text:
maria: Hey team — need to spin up a small burst GPU nodepool in europe-west4 for short-lived batch jobs (1-5 min). Constraints: subnet IP exhaustion in a/b, quota for A10G limited, and we want aggressive scale-to-zero when idle. Thoughts on instance type + taint strategy? :thinking:

sam: A10G is the sweet spot for cost vs perf for embedding workloads. If quota is tight, fallback to T4 for non-critical jobs. Use preemptible/spot for burst pools to save $$ :money_with_wings:

bao: Agreed on A10G preference. Suggest mixed-instance nodepool with taint key gpu=burst:NoSchedule so only batch pods opt-in. Tolerations on the job spec. Also set nodeSelector for instance-class if you need perf guarantees.

maria: Example toleration I was thinking: ```yaml
tolerations:
  - key: "gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "burst"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```
And nodepool taint: `gpu=burst:NoSchedule`. Good?

bao: Yep. For autoscaler config, use conservative scale-up to avoid quota spikes: `--max-node-provision-time=15m`, `balance-similar-node-groups=true`, and set `maxTotalUnreadyPercentage` low. Also cap max nodes for the pool to avoid blasting quota.

jordan: Two networking flags to watch: europe-west4 subnet has low available IPs in zone-b — suggest we mark zone-b as unschedulable for this pool (nodeAffinity to avoid zone-b) or request a subnet expansion. Also NLB egress we saw earlier hits NAT gateway port exhaustion for many short-lived pods. If we run lots of bursts, either increase NAT ports or use per-node SNAT.

kevin: On quota: we should open a consolidated quota request to cloud with the below snippet. Filing now will speed things up.
```bash
gcloud compute regions describe europe-west4 
# check quotas
gcloud compute project-info describe --project=my-project
```
Also consider a small reserved Dedicated pool if some workloads are SLA-sensitive.

maria: Good call. I don't want to move to Dedicated for these ephemeral jobs. Plan: mixed A10G(spot)/T4(spot) nodepool, tainted gpu=burst:NoSchedule, max_nodes=10, zones a/c only, scale-to-zero when idle. Will someone draft the terraform?

sam: I can do a quick terraform module. Rough snippet: ```hcl
module "gpu_burst_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra-modules.git//gke/nodepool"
  name   = "burst-a10g"
  machine_type = ["a10g", "t4"]
  preemptible  = true
  taints = [{key="gpu",value="burst",effect="NO_SCHEDULE"}]
  max_nodes = 10
  min_nodes = 0
  zones = ["europe-west4-a","europe-west4-c"]
}
```
I'll push a branch later today.

bao: Autoscaler knobs: set `--max-total-unready-percentage=20`, `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m` so we don't thrash with short jobs. For scale-to-zero, confirm your cloud provider supports removing the last node (some setups need a separate island).

jordan: On NAT: I'll open a ticket to increase per-node SNAT ports and add an egress runbook if we hit >80% NAT usage. For now, prefer longer-lived connections or batch jobs should reuse sockets if possible.

kevin: Cost note — running 10 a10g preemptible concurrently for 5 min spikes cost but still far cheaper than Dedicated. We'll add a cost alert if spend > $X/day for the pool.

infra-bot: [autoscaler-config] applied change: gpu-burst-pool autoscaler maxNodes=10 minNodes=0 zones=[a,c] taint=gpu=burst:NoSchedule — ticket INFRA-4627 created for subnet expansion.

maria: Perfect. I'll file the quota request (requesting +5 A10G and +20 T4) and assign infra-bot to the terraform PR reviews. Thanks all :raised_hands:

sam: Ping me if quota gets rejected — we can fallback to T4-only pool and reduce max_nodes.

maria: Will do. End plan: file quota, PR terraform, enable autoscaler knobs, monitor NAT. Closing once quota approved.
